title: Epochal activation spill and adaptive scratch packing to reduce GPU workspace
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce epochal activation spill and adaptive scratch packing to cut peak GPU working set (15-28% observed). Opt-in runtime flag; no public API changes.
description: Motivation: large-sequence generation and long-lived KV/activation lifetimes cause volatile peak GPU working sets due to per-kernel scratch and activation retention. This PR adds two complementary runtime optimizations: (1) epochal activation spill: group model activations into 'epochs' based on layer/lifecycle analysis and allow cold epochs to be spilled to pinned host memory with fast async DMA and rehydration heuristics; (2) adaptive scratch packing: analyze per-kernel scratch lifetimes at compile-time and coalesce small, short-lived scratch allocations into packed buckets to reduce fragmentation and per-kernel workspace overhead. Design notes: - Epochal spill is conservative by default and gated under config.runtime.epochal_spill.enabled=false to avoid surprises in private/on-prem installs. Default: off for private, enabled for hosted canaries. - Spill policy uses a recency-and-cost score combining KV cache recency and estimated rehydrate cost; low-cost epochs are spilled first. - Scratch packing introduces a packing-bucket allocator layered on top of the existing arena. Buckets are keyed by alignment and expected lifetime class (short/medium/long). Packing is adaptive: the runtime observes allocation histograms over short windows and rebalances bucket sizes. - Continuous batching scheduler tweaks prioritize packing-favorable batch orderings and prefer lower inter-kernel scratch variance in a batch to reduce temporary high-water marks. - KV-cache eviction is augmented with a 'windowed hotset' score that biases eviction away from recently accessed token windows and layers with high reuse. Implementation summary: - runtime/arena/packed_allocator.{h,cc}: new bucketed allocator plus eviction hooks. - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cc: integrate packing hints and batch ordering heuristics. - runtime/kv/evict_policy.cc: windowed_hotset scorer and metrics. - runtime/activation/spill_manager.{h,cc}: epochal grouping, async spill/reload, warmup prefetch on predicted next-window accesses. - build targets and unit/perf tests added under test/runtime and perf/benchmarks/epochal_spill. Benchmarks (internal; averaged over 5 runs): - LLaMA-2-70B, seq=8192: peak GPU working set reduced by 22% (from 38.1GB -> 29.7GB); end-to-end latency change +3% p50, p99 +6% in worst case rehydrate path; throughput sustained within 2% of baseline for batch sizes >1. - GPT-like 13B, seq=4096: peak reduced 15%, latency impact <1.5%. Rollout: staged canary on dedicated pools with epochal_spill.enabled=true for low-util regions; monitor new metrics: runtime_epoch_spill_count, runtime_spill_latency_ms, gpu_peak_working_set_bytes, scratch_pack_ratio. Opt-out plan: config.runtime.epochal_spill.enabled=false or spill_threshold_bytes override. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes; all config flags are runtime-only. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-4821) - [x] unit tests for allocator and spill manager - [x] perf benchmarks and regression suite - [x] metrics and dashboards - [x] canary rollout plan - [x] docs/notes on tunables Changes are intentionally conservative in heuristics to limit regressions; trade-offs are documented in ENG-4821.

review_comments: Marco Li (2026-01-28): Overall looks promising. Two questions: (1) can we quantify worst-case rehydrate latency and expose a config knob? (2) how does packing interact with existing slab arenas? Please add unit tests that simulate fragmentation patterns.

Aisha Patel (2026-01-28): Added config.runtime.spill_rehydrate_timeout_ms and the packing layer falls back to slab arenas when buckets are under pressure. Expanded tests to include synthetic fragmentation patterns (test/runtime/packed_allocator_test.cc).

Dana Schultz (2026-01-30): CI showed an intermittent failure in the packed allocator stress test on CUDA-12.2. Root cause: race in free-list rebuild. Please add a short sleep or reorder atomic ops to be deterministic.
Aisha Patel (2026-01-31): Fixed race by making free-list rebuild idempotent and added a deterministic stress harness. Reran CI; green.

Priya Nair (2026-02-01): Verified perf numbers on dedicated canary pool. Observed expected peak reduction but saw two regression traces where rehydrate overlapped with another large allocation and caused a transient OOM in an older driver. Recommendation: guard async spill with a runtime driver-quirks table. I'll approve after a guard is added.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-02): Added driver-quirks guard and fallback to immediate allocation path when pinned host DMA is unreliable. Addressed Priya's comment and squashed commits for merge.
notes: Canary rollout scheduled: 2026-02-05 to dedicated:us-west-2, dedicated:eu-west-1
Config flag: runtime.epochal_spill.enabled (default: false for private, true in hosted canary), runtime.spill_threshold_bytes, runtime.spill_rehydrate_timeout_ms
New metrics: runtime_epoch_spill_count, runtime_spill_latency_ms, scratch_pack_ratio, gpu_peak_working_set_bytes
Follow-ups: auto-tuning of bucket sizes (ENG-4922), deeper integration with quantization runtimes (ENG-4990)
